clue.text: Place to park behind station

blocks.note: first meaning: somewhere to rest one's bottom
second meaning: a position or post

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like directions to a car park behind a railway station, but 'park' is to sit and 'behind' is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is where you rest your rear, and Chambers also lists the word as a position or post one occupies.

clue.text: Couple given months for putting up a small child

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a couple is two
MS is the abbreviation for months

explanation.surface: Parents are given a few months to raise a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' sounds like housing or raising a child; here it turns the letters upside down in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: SMOWT is a Scots word, also spelt smout, for a little person or youngster, given in Chambers.

clue.text: Beaten in Toulouse? That's satisfactory but record time taken

indicators.note: things taken away are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: satisfactory means good enough
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A rugby fan admits a defeat in Toulouse was fine, though the match ran long.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E, P and T from ACCEPTABLE. The question mark flags that the definition is French: accablé means overwhelmed.
explanation.definitionFit: In French accablé means overwhelmed or crushed, and Chambers keeps the word in an older English sense of overpowered.

clue.text: Southerner disheartened old Greek

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central letter of the word

blocks.note: a Texan is from a southern US state

explanation.surface: A man from the Deep South feels downcast beside an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: TEXAN loses its middle X.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tean was a native of Teos, an ancient Ionian city; the poet Anacreon is called the Tean.

clue.text: One inclined to go wrong could be a faceless jihadi

indicators.note: without a face means without its front, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a jihadi fighter could be called this

explanation.surface: Someone prone to going astray could become an anonymous militant.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRORIST loses its first letter T. 'Could be' marks the jihadi as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers has errorist as one who errs or encourages error, a person given to mistakes.

clue.text: Young partner in finance managed rents

indicators.note: managed letters are handled and reorganised into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A junior partner in a money business looked after the property rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an age, but it is the surname Young: Ernst & Young is the big accountancy firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The accountancy firm Ernst & Young pairs the two founders' names, so Ernst is Young's partner in that finance business.

clue.text: Batter's role in defence

blocks.note: a ram is a battering beast or engine; the 's is just the possessive
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman's job in a defensive innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' suggests cricket or baseball; here it is something that batters, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive earth wall or embankment around a fort.

clue.text: Party absorbed by Bojo's latest bombast that's created a stink

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that makes a smell

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its final letter
what is absorbed is soaked up inside the other pieces

blocks.note: last letter of Bojo, Boris Johnson's nickname
a do is a party
bombast is ranting talk

explanation.surface: A party swallowed by Boris Johnson's latest bluster caused a political row.
explanation.walkthrough: Bojo is the press nickname of former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson; 'stink' suggests a scandal, but the definition is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An odorant is any substance that gives off a smell, so it is what creates a stink.

clue.text: Persian verse brings in tense distorted rhythms

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a rubai is a Persian quatrain, as in the Rubaiyat
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A Persian poem uses strained, uneven metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubati is the plural of rubato, the musical freedom of stretching and squeezing tempo.

clue.text: Cooking ingredient Indonesian chief gets in markets

indicators.note: getting in means entering and sitting inside something else

blocks.note: sales are markets for goods
a ratu is a chief or ruler in Indonesia and Fiji

explanation.surface: An Indonesian ruler buys a spice at the bazaar.
explanation.definitionFit: Saleratus is sodium bicarbonate used as a raising agent in baking, a kitchen ingredient.

clue.text: Staff managed to trim a Brazilian tree

blocks.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
ran a business means managed it
Chambers gives dub as to trim or dress, as with a cock's comb
taken as written

explanation.surface: Staff managed to prune a tree in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed' looks like a verb with 'to trim' following, but each word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Maceranduba is a hardwood timber tree of Brazil, related to the milk tree.

clue.text: University official in bubble tackling education

indicators.note: tackling here means grappling with and wrapping round, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: Chambers lists bell as a bubble
ED is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: A university administrator in a protected bubble deals with schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubble' suggests a sheltered world; it is the rare sense of bell as a bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedell is the Oxford and Cambridge spelling of beadle, a ceremonial university officer.

clue.text: Veteran Italian is old judge no longer employed

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an obsolete noun sense of scan is judgement

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian is a retired magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer employed' looks like retirement, but it marks the sense of scan as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscan was the language and people of ancient southern Italy, so an Oscan is a very old Italian.

clue.text: City sort of home for the rabble

definitions.text: sort of home for the rabble

blocks.note: first meaning: a port city in Alabama

blocks.clueFragment: sort of home for the rabble
blocks.note: second meaning: the kind of home on wheels, and also an old word for the mob

explanation.walkthrough: The second part does double duty: it is a mobile home, and the word in Chambers also means the mob, the rabble.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobile is an Alabama city, a mobile home is a caravan-style dwelling, and the mobile is an old term for the common people.

clue.text: Question about Saigon hospital being organised for malaria treatment

indicators.note: organised letters are put into a new arrangement
about means surrounding, so these letters go round the rest

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for question
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Questions surround a Saigon hospital setting up malaria care.
explanation.walkthrough: SAIGON plus H is rearranged and placed between Q and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Qinghaosu is the Chinese name for artemisinin, the sweet wormwood extract used against malaria.

clue.text: Soldier's half-hearted action displayed

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, one of the two middle letters is lost

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper; the 's is just the possessive
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A soldier's lukewarm effort was put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: DEED drops one of its central Es.
explanation.definitionFit: To parade something is to show it off, so paraded means displayed.

clue.text: Cat runs away from goat's-hair fabric

indicators.note: something that runs away leaves, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Tibert is the cat in the Reynard the Fox fables
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cat flees from a woolly goat-hair cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs away' reads as a whole phrase, but runs is R and 'away from' signals removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet is a cloth originally made from goat's hair, named after the region.

clue.text: Former probes are confidential

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Past investigations are kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A latere, Latin for from the side, describes a papal legate who is a trusted confidant.

clue.text: Taking day off, two places of seclusion being discussed

indicators.note: taking something off means removing it from the word

blocks.note: a den and a lair are both hideaways
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Taking a day's leave, a pair of secluded retreats are under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: DEN plus LAIR loses its D. 'Taking ... off' wraps the letter being removed.
explanation.definitionFit: En l'air is French for in the air, and an idea in the air is being talked about.

clue.text: Heat extremes stop Middle East project

indicators.note: here stop means put a stop to, cutting those letters out
heated letters are agitated and stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East

explanation.surface: Extreme temperatures halt a Middle East building scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' looks like a noun but is a verb acting on EXTREMES, which loses M and E before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Exsert is a botanical verb meaning to thrust out or stick out, so to project.

clue.text: Where you may find a cuckoo being most silly

definitions.text: Where you may find a cuckoo

blocks.clueFragment: Where you may find a cuckoo
blocks.note: first meaning, read as three words: inside someone else's bird home
second meaning: the superlative of foolish

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer 2,1,4 to get the place a cuckoo chick sits; a cuckoo is also a fool, which makes the pair neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or foolish, so the superlative form is the most silly.

clue.text: Cords perhaps getting fashionable in Surrey town

blocks.note: bags are loose trousers, and corduroys are an example
hot means in fashion

explanation.surface: Corduroy trousers are becoming trendy in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south-west of London; cords are corduroy trousers and bags is British slang for baggy trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagshot is a village-sized town in Surrey, England, near Camberley.

clue.text: Jam rolls are small and special for a little girl

indicators.note: to roll here is to wrap up, so the outer piece enfolds the rest

blocks.note: a lock, as in gridlock, is a jam
A is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area
S is the abbreviation for small
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Jam rolls are a small, special treat for a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam rolls' looks like a cake; jam is a traffic lock, and 'rolls' means wraps round. 'Are' is the metric unit of area.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassock is a Scots diminutive of lass, meaning a young girl.

clue.text: Head of Music Society welcomes a Scottish bar that's taken up thumb pianos

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
to welcome is to take in, so this piece holds the others
in a down entry, taken up means lifted so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: first letter of Music
taken as written
in Scotland a rib is a bar of a fire grate
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A music society chief welcomes a Scottish pub that has bought thumb pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a grate bar. A plus RIB is turned upward and sits inside M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An mbira is an African instrument of metal tongues plucked with the thumbs, also called a thumb piano.

clue.text: Amateur covering of trial repeatedly gets stick in US

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for amateur
outer letters of trial
the three letters so far are written a second time

explanation.surface: An amateur's trial outfit keeps getting stuck in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlatl is a Native American spear-throwing stick from Mexico and the American Southwest.

clue.text: House report is behind small reorganisation of Health and Safety Executive

indicators.note: a minor reorganisation rearranges these few letters into another order
being behind means coming after, so this piece goes at the end

blocks.note: HSE is the UK workplace safety regulator
a report is the sound of a gun, a bang

explanation.surface: A government report follows a shake-up at the British workplace safety body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' sounds like a document, but it is the sound of a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives shebang as a hut, shop or dwelling, an American slang word for a house.

clue.text: Salmon farm in Provence near me

indicators.note: near means placed beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: a mas is a farmhouse in southern France
us is used for me in colloquial and royal speech

explanation.surface: A fish farm in the south of France not far from where I live.
explanation.walkthrough: Provence is a region of southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The masu is a Pacific salmon of Japan; like the word fish, salmon here serves as a plural.

clue.text: What's dividing leaders in Mali, Djibouti and Iraq? Not me, I'm a great leader

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters
dividing means splitting the other letters apart by sitting between them

blocks.note: first letters of Mali, Djibouti and Iraq
eh? is said when asking what

explanation.surface: A dictator asks what divides African and Middle East leaders, and denies blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not me' is a protest in the surface; the definition is the speaker claiming to be the awaited leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mehdi is a variant of Mahdi, the messianic guide expected in Islam, so a great spiritual leader.

clue.text: Alternatively part of spiral canal (obscure noun)

definitions.text: Alternatively part of spiral canal (obscure noun)

indicators.note: only a part of the word is used, here its opening letter
to obscure is to hide from view, so that letter is removed
an alternative arrangement means the letters are put in another order

blocks.note: first letter of spiral
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A note that a term for a section of a spiral duct is an alternative, little-known noun.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus CANAL loses N and is rearranged. The whole clue also describes the answer, one of the spiral canals of the inner ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scala is the anatomical name for each of the spiral passages of the cochlea, such as the scala tympani.

clue.text: Environment Agency calls for small ropes

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for the UK's Environment Agency
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A government environment body asks for thin cords.
explanation.definitionFit: Earings are the short ropes fastening the upper corners of a sail to the yard, a nautical term.

clue.text: Jackdaw flying around one in disused wharf

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: kae is a Scots word for a jackdaw; flying just adds to the picture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jackdaw' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the answer is the wharf.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaie is an obsolete spelling of quay, a landing place for ships, so a wharf no longer in use as a word.

clue.text: Bad error to ride a sick horse

indicators.note: something bad is wrong, so these letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A roarer is a horse with a breathing disorder that makes it wheeze noisily when exercised.

clue.text: Nothing stops nurse returning for a drink

a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an amah is a nurse or nanny in East Asia

clue.text: Erratic Conservative PM said nothing's wrong? A lie that's put out

wrong means not right, so the letters go into a new order

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written
taken as written
O for nothing, with the S of the contraction
taken as written
taken as written
i.e. is short for id est, that is

clue.text: Marmoset indeed in France seen alongside second small tree

clue.text: Fan yakked about uncovered one-horse carriage

blocks.note: surface padding: it only supplies a chatterer for the story
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' only sets the scene of someone chattering; the wordplay is the next word with its ends cut and turned round.
